subject: firefighting
intro: Firefighting leads into the protective service: the crews on the engine, the investigators who read a fire's cause, the medics on the ambulance, and the crews that strip hazards out of buildings.

roles.title: Firefighters
roles.what: Control and extinguish fires and respond to emergencies where life, property or the environment is at risk, with duties spanning fire suppression, emergency medical response, search and rescue and hazardous-material incidents.
roles.where: The NFPA 1001 units are the job description: fire behaviour and flashover, turnout gear and SCBA air management, hose lines and water supply, ladders, ventilation and forcible entry.

roles.title: Fire Inspectors and Investigators
roles.what: Detect fire hazards by inspecting buildings and enforcing fire codes, and investigate fires and explosions to determine their cause and origin.
roles.where: Unit 1's fire behaviour — combustion, growth, flashover, smoke and backdraft — is the science of reading a fire scene, and unit 6's prevention and inspection topics are the enforcement half of the role.

roles.title: Paramedics
roles.what: Administer advanced emergency medical care at the scene and in transit: assess injuries and illness, give medication intravenously, and provide advanced life support to sick and injured people.
roles.where: Unit 5's rescue and medical operations — search and rescue, extrication and patient care under pressure — is the fire-service gateway into EMS, and unit 2's rehab and air management keeps crews and patients alive.

roles.title: Hazardous Materials Removal Workers
roles.what: Find, contain and remove hazardous materials such as asbestos, lead and radioactive or chemical contaminants, working in protective suits under strict containment procedures.
roles.where: Unit 6's hazardous-materials awareness and unit 2's PPE discipline are the baseline of abatement work, extended by unit 1's understanding of combustion and the products of fire.
